ICST Artist in Residence from **16.06.2025 to 06.07.2025** (Studio-Residence)

During his three-week ICST Studio Residency, Nandele Maguni produced a new release entitled “Kampfumo” based on his field recordings from Maputo.
![nandele_01](nandele_01.png)

### Exploring Sound at ZHdK – ICST

Being in residency at ZHdK – Zurich University of the Arts, within the ICST, has been an inspiring experience.

I'm currently developing the project Kampfumo, a sonic exploration based on the everyday soundscape of Maputo, especially the Chapa 100 transport system and the vibrant energy of the Kampfumo district.

At the ICST spatial audio studio, I’m experimenting with immersive technologies to create a cinematic and multidimensional listening experience.
### Listen to the new release from Nandele Maguni:
- [Nandele Maguni "Kampfumo" Stereo](https://e.pcloud.link/publink/show?code=XZcB96ZIpQd93jYp9YJyyVLT0aWOSThvLNV)
- [Nandele Maguni "Kampfumo" Binaural](https://e.pcloud.link/publink/show?code=XZk296ZezHI5GUzScpbYWV0SADkCjkigCbV)
- [Nandele Maguni "Kampfumo" Binaural+ ](https://e.pcloud.link/publink/show?code=XZV296ZHgMAiKBRIB0EGXgbV9g5V0hDomjk)
  
- (Binaural+ is like in Home Cinema)

This is not just about sound but movement, memory, and space.  
![nandele_02](nandele_02.png)

ICST Artist in Residence from **16.06.2025 to 06.07.2025** (Studio-Residence)

During his three-week ICST Studio Residency, Nandele Maguni produced a new release entitled “Kampfumo” based on his field recordings from Maputo.
![nandele_01](nandele_01.png)

### Exploring Sound at ZHdK – ICST

Being in residency at ZHdK – Zurich University of the Arts, within the ICST, has been an inspiring experience.

I'm currently developing the project Kampfumo, a sonic exploration based on the everyday soundscape of Maputo, especially the Chapa 100 transport system and the vibrant energy of the Kampfumo district.

At the ICST spatial audio studio, I’m experimenting with immersive technologies to create a cinematic and multidimensional listening experience.

# Ana Gonzalez Gamboa


ICST Artist in Residence from **08.09.2025 to 16.09.2025** 
(Studio-Residence)
![Ana Gonzalez](GOPR4281.jpg)

“Lúmina” is a composition that intertwines travel recordings with fragments of anime, constructing an imaginary world where memory and fiction intersect, a borderless space that emerges with the fluidity of a dream, where the everyday is transformed and the imaginary acquires the texture of the real. 

Among these recordings are sounds from my journey to Nuevo Rocafuerte, a small town in the Ecuadorian Amazon on the banks of the Napo River, near the border with Peru. I arrived there after a 15-hour boat trip, surrounded by rain, birds, and the calls of exotic animals that became my companions.

In this work, I reflect on the interaction between soundscapes, human presence, and daily life—considering sound as both a form of communication and a way of constructing meaning in space and time. By listening to the town as if it were an instrument, with its own parameters of pitch, rhythm, intensity, timbre, and duration, these recordings merge with other sonic materials to create a dynamic and mutable soundscape.

Based in Buenos Aires  and born in Ambato, Ecuador, Ana Gamboa is a cellist, composer, and sound artist whose work explores the hybridity of acoustic and electronic practices. Since 2018, she has been building a personal archive of sounds from her travels across Latin America, intertwining them with collaborative improvisation and experimental composition. Her practice investigates memory, identity, and the imaginary through sound.

Web: [https://anagonzalezgamboa0.wixsite.com/anagamboa](https://anagonzalezgamboa0.wixsite.com/anagamboa)

ICST Artist in Residence from **16.06.2025 to 06.07.2025** (Studio-Residence)

During his three-week ICST Studio Residency, Nandele Maguni produced a new release entitled “Kampfumo” based on his field recordings from Maputo.
![nandele_01](nandele_01.png)

### Exploring Sound at ZHdK – ICST

Being in residency at ZHdK – Zurich University of the Arts, within the ICST, has been an inspiring experience.

I'm currently developing the project Kampfumo, a sonic exploration based on the everyday soundscape of Maputo, especially the Chapa 100 transport system and the vibrant energy of the Kampfumo district.

At the ICST spatial audio studio, I’m experimenting with immersive technologies to create a cinematic and multidimensional listening experience.
### Listen to the new release from Nandele Maguni:
- [Nandele Maguni "Kampfumo" Stereo](https://e.pcloud.link/publink/show?code=XZcB96ZIpQd93jYp9YJyyVLT0aWOSThvLNV)

- [Nandele Maguni "Kampfumo" Binaural+ ](https://e.pcloud.link/publink/show?code=XZV296ZHgMAiKBRIB0EGXgbV9g5V0hDomjk)

This is not just about sound but movement, memory, and space.

# Ana Gonzalez Gamboa


ICST Artist in Residence from **08.09.2025 to 16.09.2025** 
(Studio-Residence)
![Ana Gonzalez](GOPR4281.jpg)

“Lúmina” is a composition that intertwines travel recordings with fragments of anime, constructing an imaginary world where memory and fiction intersect, a borderless space that emerges with the fluidity of a dream, where the everyday is transformed and the imaginary acquires the texture of the real. 

Among these recordings are sounds from my journey to Nuevo Rocafuerte, a small town in the Ecuadorian Amazon on the banks of the Napo River, near the border with Peru. I arrived there after a 15-hour boat trip, surrounded by rain, birds, and the calls of exotic animals that became my companions.

In this work, I reflect on the interaction between soundscapes, human presence, and daily life—considering sound as both a form of communication and a way of constructing meaning in space and time. By listening to the town as if it were an instrument, with its own parameters of pitch, rhythm, intensity, timbre, and duration, these recordings merge with other sonic materials to create a dynamic and mutable soundscape.

Based in Buenos Aires  and born in Ambato, Ecuador, Ana Gamboa is a cellist, composer, and sound artist whose work explores the hybridity of acoustic and electronic practices. Since 2018, she has been building a personal archive of sounds from her travels across Latin America, intertwining them with collaborative improvisation and experimental composition. Her practice investigates memory, identity, and the imaginary through sound.

- Toni-Areal, Kompositionsstudio 3.D02, Ebene 3,
- Pfingstweidstrasse 96, Zürich

_Free admission_

---

At ICST we have launched a pilot project to enable the best possible and simple access to electroacoustic works. This idea is derived from the writings and techniques of Michael Gerzon and his team, that B-format in ambisonics is ideally suited for this.

## Objective:

B-format as a platform for dealing with immersive audio, not only in composition/production, but in the handling of existing repertoire.

- Interpretation
- Processing as immersive audio
- Archiving in B-format

## Advantages:

- A file format that 'B-format ambiX' from which any other common format can be derived.
- A file format for archiving together with metadata.
- Not dependent on short-term commercial format hype.

## Experiment:

(Listening examples)

Stereo tape compositions:
- Judy Klein (*1943): "The Wolves of Bays Mountain" for 2-channel tape (1998)
- Georg Katzer (1935-2019): "Aide-mémoire" for 2-channel tape (1983)

Quadrophonic
- Jean-Claude Risset (1938-2016) "Songes" for 4-channel tape (1979)

Eight-channel
- Jonathan Harvey (1939-2012): "Mortus Plango, Vivos Voco" for eight-channel tape (1980)
- Various versions

Ambisonics UHJ
- Maurice Ravel "Pavane pour une Infante défunte", Vlado Perlemuter, piano (Nimbus release in UHJ (2-channel/stereo compatible), 1977)

Ambisonics recording (B-format OA1)
- Ensemble peregrina at Heiligkreuz, Binningen/Basel (2025)

---

Each example will be presented in three different versions:
- Original Format
- Ambisonics
- Ambisonics UpScaled mit ICST MultiDecoder

Presentation: Johannes Schütt

---

©2025 ICST

    25→
    26→At ICST we have launched a pilot project to enable the best possible and simple access to electroacoustic works. This idea is derived from the writings and techniques of Michael Gerzon and his team, that B-format in ambisonics is ideally suited for this.
    27→
    28→## Objective:
    29→
    30→B-format as a platform for dealing with immersive audio, not only in composition/production, but in the handling of existing repertoire.
    31→
    32→- Interpretation
    33→- Processing as immersive audio
    34→- Archiving in B-format
    35→
    36→## Advantages:
    37→
    38→- A file format that 'B-format ambiX' from which any other common format can be derived.
    39→- A file format for archiving together with metadata.
    40→- Not dependent on short-term commercial format hype.
    41→
    42→## Experiment:
    43→
    44→(Listening examples)
    45→
    46→Stereo tape compositions:
    47→- Judy Klein (*1943): "The Wolves of Bays Mountain" for 2-channel tape (1998)
    48→- Georg Katzer (1935-2019): "Aide-mémoire" for 2-channel tape (1983)
    49→

    52→

    55→- Various versions
    56→

    15→## **Listening Twice**
    16→
    17→**Experiment**

    20→- Toni-Areal, Kompositionsstudio 3.D02, Ebene 3,

    25→---
    26→
    27→"Listening Twice"
    28→
    29→In this listening session, we want to engage with ambisonics UHJ recordings from the seventies. UHJ, also called C-format, is a hierarchical system for encoding and decoding directional sound information within ambisonics technology. Although UHJ allows up to four channels, mostly only the 2-channel variant has been and is used, since this ensures full compatibility with 2-channel playback media (usually stereo records or CDs). With a special UHJ decoder, the three channels LRT (corresponding to W, X, Y) can be played back in Ambisonics as spatial audio. We want to compare the various playback options together by listening using various historical recordings.
    30→

     2→title: Step by Step Setup
     3→date: 2025-01-23T15:38:00
     4→---
     5→Institute for Computer Music and Sound Technology / (ICST) Zurich University of the Arts
     6→
     7→---
     8→# Step-by-Step Setup Guide for the ICST AmbiPlugins in Reaper
     9→
    10→---
    11→### Prerequisites
    12→
    13→Before we begin, make sure you have **Reaper**, the **ICST Ambisonics plugins** and any recommended **3rd party plugins**installed.
    14→
    15→### Creating a Reaper template
    16→
    17→We will create the template step by step from top to bottom.
    18→
    19→#### 1. Prepare Reaper
    20→
    21→1. Open a **new, empty Reaper session**.
    22→    ![empty_reaper](empty_reaper.png)
    23→2. Create a new track (**double click** or use the menu).
    24→3. Name the track **Decoder** and remove the master bus.
    25→    ![01_dec](01_Decoder_A.gif)
    26→
    27→> [!Tip:]
    28→>  Create all tracks with **64 channels** by default and keep an eye on the **routing**.
    29→
    30→#### 2. Set up decoder routing
    31→
    32→-  **Decoder routing for an Oktagon setup:**
    33→- **Inputs:** 64 channels from the “Bformat Master Track”  
    34→- **outputs**: 8 channels to the audio interface
    35→1. **ICST AmbiPlugins Decoder** in the **FX window**.
    36→   ![open__FX_decoder](FX_Decoder.png)
    37→2. open the AmbiDecoder
    38→   ![open_decoder](open_decoder.gif)
    39→3. Select a **speaker preset** (e.g. Oktagon).
    40→    ![open_dec](choose_dec_preset.gif)
    41→4. **Customize AmbiDecoder settings**:
    42→- Ambisonics Weighting
    43→- Ambisonics Order (1st to 7th order)
    44→  ![Dec-setting](7_choose_dec_setting.gif)5. **Run speaker test**:  
    45→	- press the “Speaker Test” button or test individual speakers.
    46→![speaker_test](speaker_test.png)
    47→
    48→> [!Attention:]  Keep an eye on the volume level!
    49→
    50→
    51→9. Create the 'Bformat-Master track'
    52→![02_BF-Master | 700](02_BF-Master.gif)
    53→
    54→#### 3. Create a Bformat master track
    55→
    56→- The **Bformat master track** receives all signals from:
    57→- **Ambience Encoders**
    58→- **BFormat SFX**
    59→- **BFormat players**
    60→- Since this is the master track, the final **B format is recorded** or bounced here.  
    61→- This track is colored **red**.
    62→- It leads both to the **AmbiDecoder** and in parallel to a **binaural track**.
    63→
    64→#### 4. Create a Bformat player track
    65→
    66→- Create a **64-channel track** and route it into the **Bformat master track**.
    67→
    68→![bformat-player](bformat-player.png)
    69→> [!Tip:] This allows **B-format files from the 1st to the 7th order** to be played.
    70→
    71→#### 5. Enable binaural listening
    72→
    73→- Create a new **64-channel track** and load a **binaural plug-in** (e.g. _DearVR Ambi Micro.vst3_).
    74→- Move the track **upwards**.
    75→- Route the output from the **format master** to this **binaural decoder**.
    76→- **Mute AmbiDecoder** to hear only the binaurally decoded signal.  
    77→    
    78→> [!Tip:] Compare with _Solo/Mute_ between AmbiDecoder and Binaural Decoder.
    79→
    80→
    81→![1.order_bf](first-order.png)
    82→Example B shows a 5th-order b-format Ambisonic.
    83→
    84→![5th-order_bf](5th-order-bf.png)
    85→Now we can play back and listen to B-format files on eight speakers.
    86→
    87→To be able to listen to the B format through headphones, we will now set up a binaural decoder:  
    88→- Create a new **64-channel track** and load a **binaural plugin** of your choice into the FX window (e.g. _DearVR Ambi Micro.vst3_).
    89→- Move the track **to the beginning** of the Reaper rack.
    90→- Route the **output of the Bformat master track** to this binaural decoder (see GIF).
    91→
    92→![Binaural-track](Binaural_Track.gif)
    93→- Mute the AmbiDecoder to hear only the binaurally decoded signal.
    94→![DearVR_binaural](DearVR_binaurl.png)
    95→
    96→>[!Tip:] 
    97→>Compare solo/mute between AmbiDecoder and binaural decoder.
    98→
    99→### 6. Mono Source & Ambisonics Encoder
   100→
   101→- Create a new track Mono-Source and load a mono audio file.
   102→
   103→Tip: Watch this  [Video](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=aDa-vNWriLM&t=119s)
   104→
   105→12. Mono AmbieEncoder overview.
   106→	![open monoencoder](MonoEncoder_01.png)
   107→    ![open_MonoEncoder](MonoEncoder_load.png)
   108→- In the FX window, load the ICST MonoEncoder.
   109→- Add a AmbiEncoder(ICST) (1-4) --> Mono-Encoder
   110→Routing:
   111→- MonoEncoder → 64-channel output → Bformat master.
   112→
   113→  ![MonnoEncoder](MonoEncoder.png)
   114→#### 7. Record motions in the Reaper track
   115→
   116→ Record motions in the MonoEncoder:
   117→ ![rec_xyz](rec_xyz.gif)
   118→ 
   119→ Play back saved motion:
   120→
   121→![play_xyt](play_xyz.gif)
   122→
   123→### 8. Using the Multi-Encoder
   124→
   125→In the next example, I'll demonstrate how we use the **Multi-Encoder**:
   126→
   127→1. **Insert the Multi-Encoder Track**
   128→
   129→    - Right-click in the empty Reaper track area and select **“Insert Track from Template”**.
   130→    - Navigate to **ICST AmbiPlugins** and choose **“ICST_AmbiEncoder_Multi_8src”**.
   131→    - This will open a Multi-Encoder with **8 mono sources**, already routed into the encoder.
   132→
   133→    ![MultiEncoder_routing | 550](MultiEncoder_routing.png)
   134→	2. **Controlling Sources in the Multi-Encoder**
   135→
   136→	- If the routing is set up correctly, you can now control the **placement and movement** of up to **8 sources** within the Multi-Encoder.
   137→### AmbiEncoder Settings
   138→
   139→  3. Understanding AmbiEncoder Settings**- The **AmbiEncoder settings** are crucial for your workflow. - The following GIF showcases the key **AmbiEncoder features**:  
   140→
   141→        ![Enc_Settings](Enc_Settings.gif)
   142→	 ![Enc_Settings](Enc_Settings.gif)
   143→
   144→>[!Tip: ] Watch the AmbiEncoder [Video tutorial](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=aDa-vNWriLM&t=31s)  for more details.
   145→
   146→4. **ICST Distance Function**
   147→    - A unique feature of the **ICST Ambisonics Encoder** is its **distance function**, developed by **Martin Neukom** at ICST.
   148→    - This function allows you to create various **spatial configurations**, simulating movement speeds from very fast to extremely slow.
   149→      ![Distanc_overview](Distance.gif)For in-depth instructions, refer to the **Distance tutorial**.
   150→
   151→> [!Tip:] If working with **distance**, define it **at the start** of your project to scale all **XYZ coordinates** correctly. _(Example: Distance scale from 0.0 to 1.0).
   152→
   153→### Recording & Editing Source Movements
   154→
   155→5. **Recording Movements in the Multi-Encoder**
   156→
   157→    - To understand how the Multi-Encoder works, let’s go through a **recording example**:
   158→        - **Set automation envelopes** to **“Write” mode**.
   159→        - Press **Play** (Spacebar) in Reaper and move **Src_1** in the Multi-Encoder Radar.
   160→        - Repeat the process for other sources.
   161→		
   162→		MultiEnc_01_write:
   163→     ![MultiEnc_01_write](MultiEnc_01_write.gif)
   164→     
   165→	  Here’s an example with **Src_3**:
   166→	  
   167→       ![Encoder_move_03](Move_03.gif)
   168→
   169→Here’s an example with **Src_3**:The next step demonstrates how to manually edit the xyz envelopes.
   170→![Manuel_edit](MultiEnc_Manuell_edit.gif)
   171→
   172→6. **Manually Editing XYZ Envelopes**
   173→
   174→	- To refine movements, manually adjust the **XYZ envelopes**:
   175→	- Hold **Shift** and click on the envelope to create a new edit point.
   176→	- Move the point to adjust the **XYZ coordinates**.
   177→
   178→7. Playing Back the Recorded Ambisonic Scene
   179→
   180→![MultiEnc_plays_scene](play_multienc.gif)
   181→
   182→### Working with Groups
   183→
   184→8. **Creating a Group in the Multi-Encoder**
   185→    
   186→    - In the **Radar Display**, select multiple **Src points** to form a group.
   187→    - Assign a **group name** (e.g., **G1**).
   188→
   189→![create_a_GP](GP_select_scaled.png)
   190→![GP_name](GP_edit_scaled.png)
   191→
   192→9. **Recording Group Movements**
   193→
   194→- Choose a recording mode:
   195→    - **“Latch”** – Records only one source point.
   196→    - **“Touch”** – Starts recording when a point is touched.
   197→    - **“Write”** – Overwrites previous recordings.
   198→     ![Rec_GP](Rec_GP.gif)
   199→	
   200→	9. **Playback & Evaluation**
   201→     ![Play_GP](play_GP.gif)
   202→	- Listen to the final **group movement recording** via **speakers (Decoder)** or **headphones (Binaural Decoder)**.
   203→
   204→### Finalizing & Exporting
   205→
   206→11. **Rendering the B-Format Master**
   207→	- Once satisfied, follow these steps to **export the B-Format**:
   208→	    - Select **Bformat-Master Track** and set it to **Solo**.
   209→	    - Open **Menu > Render**.
   210→
   211→**Render Settings:**
   212→
   213→  ![Render_Master | 200](render-master.png)
   214→
   215→
   216→1. **Select Track (Stem Render)** → Choose **Bformat-Master**.
   217→2. **File Name** → Assign a **B-Format filename**.
   218→3. **Sample Rate** → 48,000 kHz.
   219→4. **Channels** → 64 (for **7th-order Ambisonics**).
   220→5. **Multichannel Format** → Set to **Multichannel Files**.
   221→6. **Large File Support** → Use **Wave/RF64**.
   222→7. **Click “Render”**.
   223→
   224→Rendering-info:
   225→     ![render-info](render_info.png)
   226→		After the rendering process, you will get a Rendering Info window with the Peak and LUFS information.
   227→
   228→8. That's all, now you can drag and drop your B-Format onto the B-Format player track, set it to “Solo” and listen to the final result via the ICST decoder or the binaural decoder.
   229→
   230→
   231→🎧 Happy ambisonics!
   232→

     9→# ICST Ambisonics Plugins v3.2 
    10→
    11→_**Now Available!**_
    12→
    13→**Download:**  
    14→🔗 **GitHub Releases**  
    15→([https://github.com/schweizerweb/icst-ambisonics-plugins/releases](https://github.com/schweizerweb/icst-ambisonics-plugins/releases)
    16→
    17→# **What’s New in v3.2?**
    18→
    19→We’re pleased to announce **ICST Ambisonics Plugins v3.2**, featuring a major update to the **Multi-Decoder**, new user interface layouts, enhanced filter options, improved OSC control, and numerous workflow improvements based on ongoing empirical research at ICST.
    20→
    21→📖 **Full Documentation:**  
    22→🔗 [**Wiki**]([https://github.com/schweizerweb/icst-ambisonics-plugins/wiki](https://github.com/schweizerweb/icst-ambisonics-plugins/wiki)
    23→
    24→---
    25→# ICST AmbiDecoder v3.2
    26→
    27→## **New Features & Improvements**
    28→
    29→### Bidirectional Solo & Mute
    30→- Easily solo or mute individual loudspeakers or groups.
    31→- **Keyboard shortcuts (macOS):**  
    32→	`Shift + Control + S` / `Shift + Control + M`
    33→
    34→  ![bidi_mute](bidi_mute.gif)
    35→### Redesigned Layout
    36→A clearer and more modular structure:
    37→- **Speaker Settings**
    38→- **Decoder Settings**
    39→- **Filter Options**
    40→- **Additional Features** _(coming soon)_
    41→  ![New_layout](Layout_v3_1.png)
    42→### New CSV Export & Preset Management
    43→- Export speaker coordinates to **CSV** for use in Max (and vice versa).
    44→- Backup and export all presets as **XML**.
    45→- Import preset backups directly.
    46→
    47→![CSV](Speaker_setting_managment.gif)
    48→### Improved Filter Interface
    49→
    50→- Eight new filter options
    51→- Updated UI for easier comparison and tuning
    52→
    53→	![filters](filters.png)

- **Pierre Alexandre Tremblay**: Kein Bio-Text, nur Session-Tabelle

**ASCOLTA – #17 Upcoming**
- Kein Thema/Programm für die Sessions definiert
- Kein Ansprechpartner/Moderator genannt (andere: „Presentation: Johannes Schütt")

| Bereich | Vorschlag |
|---|---|
| **Ascolta _index.md** | Etwas mehr Beschreibung, was Ascolta ist (für Erstbesucher) |
| **2026-Seite** | Kurze Biographien für alle drei Künstler ergänzen |

| **RESIDENCY-Übersichtsseite** | Links auf 2025 UND 2026 Übersichtsseiten ergänzen |
| **Sprache** | Konsequent auf Englisch (öffentliche Seiten) |

---

### 🎵 Eli Stine — Composer Biography

Eli Stine is a composer, programmer, and educator. Stine received Ph.D. and Masters degrees in Composition and Computer Technologies as a Jefferson Fellow at the University of Virginia, and bachelor's degrees in Technology In Music And Related Arts and Computer Science from Oberlin College and Oberlin Conservatory.

Stine is a Visiting Assistant Professor at Oberlin Conservatory (2019–present).

---

### 🏆 Prix CIME 2025

Stine's work *Where Water Meets Memory* has been programmed internationally, was a winner of the **2025 Prix CIME Electroacoustic Music Competition**, and was a finalist for the 2022 Métamorphoses International Acousmatic Composition Contest.

The Prix CIME itself is a prestigious international competition: the International Confederation of Electroacoustic Music's biennial Prix CIME International Electroacoustic Music Competition.

---

### 🎼 Artistic Work & Research

Stine's work explores electroacoustic sound, multimedia technologies (often custom-built software, video projection, and multi-channel speaker systems), and collaboration between disciplines (artistic and otherwise).

Festivals and conferences that have programmed Stine's work include the International Computer Music Conference, Society for Electroacoustic Music in the United States conference, New Interfaces for Musical Expression conference, the International Sound Art Festival Berlin, the London Film Festival, Helsinki Design Week, Bang on a Can's LOUD Weekend, and many others.

Residencies attended include the Stanford Music Information Retrieval Workshop, Atlantic Center for the Arts, Banff Centre, Harvestworks, Prague Film School, the Spatial Music Workshop, and Centro Mexicano para la Música y las Artes Sonoras.

This work has been mentioned in publications including *USA Today*, *The Economist*, and on NPR.

---

### 🔬 Current Projects

Currently, Stine is working on releasing a set of audio plug-ins inspired by his dissertation work (EcoBaubles) and an immersive spatial audio experience in partnership with Genelec.

---

For more information, you can visit his official website at [elistine.com](https://elistine.com).

     7→
     8→* * *
     9→
    10→### Regulations for the use of the ICST composition studio:
    11→
    12→* **Do not eat or drink in the studio.**
    13→* **do not set up your own user accounts on the composition computer**
    14→* **no installation of own software & plugins (if needed, please contact support)**
    15→* **Do not move the 18-Ambisonics speakers as they have been precisely calibrated.**
    16→* **Please dismantle all modifications**
    17→* **No stock**
    18→* **Put instruments/music stands/special equipment away again.**
    19→* **Reset the audio matrix routing to 'standard.'**
    20→* **Set 'Ghielmetti' back to 'Standard'.**
    21→* **Turn off all equipment when leaving the studio.**
    22→
    23→### Important.
    24→
    25→* **The user data on the composition computer will be deleted.**
    26→* **Each user is responsible for the security of their own data. (Save to your own HD)**
    27→* **Please leave the studio in default settings when leaving!**
    28→
    29→### New:
    30→
    31→* **For night sessions, please note that the Studio components will automatically shut down at 03:00.**
    32→* **At 03:00, a warning appears on the 'Extron TouchPanel,' and with the confirmation to cancel, this process can be stopped.**
    33→
    34→**These regulations are valid for the duration of the studio booking. For projects and AiR guests, the agreed regulations are valid.**
    35→**The next studio user will thank them.**
    36→
    37→* * *
    38→©2025 ICST
